newsitem.title: UK: London gold trades quietly ahead of Christmas.
newsitem.headline: London gold trades quietly ahead of Christmas.

text.p: Precious metals business was very quiet on Monday morning and featured little more than dealers closing out positions ahead of the Christmas holiday.
"The chances of something happening are relatively slim but, because of that, if there is a move it could be quite vicious," a dealer said.
After Tuesday morning, there will be no gold fix until Friday following London's two-day Christmas holiday.
Gold was fixed at $368.70 per ounce, compared with $369.00 on Friday afternoon, after a moderately lower trend guided prices a few cents lower through the weekend.
Tokyo was closed for a national holiday leaving only light two-way business to be done in Hong Kong.
Dealers said the OTC option expiry went off quietly on Friday without creating waves or adding to volatility.
They said the market had run its course for the year and there was little likelihood of a move away from the current $368-$370 range.

"But I'm quite happy to close out positions ahead of Christmas rather than risk it getting jumpy in New York on Thursday (when London is closed)," one dealer said, adding that prices might well be different from now by Friday.
Silver was quiet as well with the price static at $4.83/$4.85, unchanged.
"There is a chance they may try to move it lower, in which case $4.78 would be the floor. You always expect silver to be more potentially volatile than gold," a dealer said.

Platinum and palladium were either side of Friday's closing levels with platinum 75 cents firmer at $372.75/$373.75 after the settling of Russia's budget hinted at a less urgent need to sell precious metals next year, and palladium was down 50 cents at $118.00/$119.00.
